To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The onset of hepatic DNA synthesis following a single injection (50 mg/kg) of cocaine is preceded by a period of hepatic damage.

the proliferative response of the mouse liver following cocaine administration occurs in a temporal and spatial sequence, and that the sequence of events following the administration of a hepatotoxin can be monitored by measuring the kinetics of the proliferative response.
the onset of hepatic cell proliferation in response to cocaine hepatotoxicity is temporally and spatially distinct from the onset of cell damage and dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a variety of hepatotoxins on hepatic function and proliferation.
the temporal and spatial sequence events which occur in the mouse liver following the administration of a single dose of cocaine.
the temporal sequence and spatial distribution of events in the liver of mice following the administration of a hepatotoxin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cocaine is a hepatotoxin which causes necrosis and subsequent proliferation.
the liver is able to respond to a hepatotoxin by proliferative renewal of hepatic function.
cocaine induces a hepatotoxin‐induced proliferative response which is initiated at 48 hr PI and completed within 96 hr PI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hepatotoxicity of cocaine is associated with a transient loss of function, but that the liver is able to recover from the insult by undergoing a period of cell proliferation.
the hepatotoxicity induced by a single injection of 150 mg/kg cocaine in mice results in a rapid onset of cell necrosis followed by a delayed proliferation of surviving cells.
the liver is capable of a rapid recovery from the effects of cocaine, and this is accomplished through the process of regeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cocaine can induce a proliferative response in the liver of mice.
cocaine‐induced hepatocyte damage is followed by proliferation and restoration of normal function.
cocaine‐induced hepatotoxicity in mice is a biphasic response with an early, acute necrotic phase and a subsequent, regenerative phase.
